Thor Tools is made for the AYN Thor and also runs on the Odin 2. On other devices it can change settings the device doesn\'t expect. Continue at your own risk.

Keeps the battery between two levels while the Thor stays plugged in, which is easier on it. At the top level AYN\'s charging separation turns on: the charger runs the Thor and the battery rests. At the bottom level charging starts again.

Each switch is a charge setting change, which owners link to unstable charging. If the stability alert shows up after a switch, restart. A charger too weak to run the Thor drains the battery while it rests.
AYN\'s 80 %% charge limit is on, so charging stops at 80 %% and the top level (%1$d %%) is never reached. Pick 80 %% or less, or turn AYN\'s limit off in AYN\'s settings.
Charging separation means the power goes straight to the device, bypassing the battery. Notice that if the power source is insufficient, battery drain will occur.

Some Thors get stuck while plugged in: the status keeps switching between Charging rapidly, Charging slowly and Not charging, and the battery charges slowly or not at all. Many owners report it, often after a charge setting changed (AYN\'s 80 % limit, charging separation, a charge limit). A restart fixes it until it happens again. This alert notices the switching and offers the restart.
What helps, from owner reports: restart after changing a charge setting; a USB-C PD charger of 27 W or more and a good cable; charge to 100 % once before turning on a charge limit.
What\'s normal: with a charge limit, charging stops at the limit and starts again below it. On a computer\'s USB port (about 2 W) the Thor says Charging but barely gains while it\'s in use.

Like a pedal: the game feels how far you pull, from a light touch to all the way. Example: easing onto the gas in a racing game.
Like a button: pressed or not, nothing in between. Example: shooting in a shooter, or ZL and ZR in a Switch emulator.
Pedal and button at once; each game uses what it understands. Example: a racing game whose menus want a click. A safe pick if you\'re not sure.
Buttons go by position, like on an Xbox pad: the bottom button is A, the right one is B. Example: most Android games and game streaming.
Each button sends the letter printed on it (A on the right, like Nintendo pads). Example: Switch and other Nintendo emulators.
Games see no controller from the Thor. Example: a game you play by touch that gets confused by a controller. You may need the touch screen to switch back.
